decisions.context: Millions of incoming documents and strong seasonal volume swings make ingestion throughput and load handling central. The brief gives no latency target.

alternatives.label: Data ingestion in batches
pros: Seasonal capacity: collect and schedule batches
cons: Freshness: results wait for the batch

alternatives.label: Data ingestion by request
cons: High daily volume: repeated retrieval overhead

decisions.rationale: High daily volume and seasonal swings decide in favor of batch intake, which supports scheduled capacity. This gives up immediate processing; the brief does not require low latency.
consequences: Results become available after batch processing.
Batch scheduling must accommodate seasonal peaks.

decisions.decision: Should data be processed in batches or in real time?
decisions.context: The classifier must handle millions of documents daily, with load that varies over the year. No real-time service level is specified.

alternatives.label: Batch-based data processing
cons: Freshness: results wait for a batch

alternatives.label: Real-time, stream-based data processing
cons: Seasonal capacity: ongoing demand as volume changes

decisions.rationale: High daily volume and seasonal swings decide in favor of scheduled batch processing. The trade-off is slower result availability, which the brief does not constrain with a latency target.
consequences: Classification results arrive after a processing run.
Capacity must be planned for seasonal peaks.

decisions.decision: How should data processing be parallelized?
decisions.context: Processing millions of documents makes parallel work relevant, and seasonal volume swings make the ability to scale throughput important.

alternatives.label: Data partitioning in data pipeline
pros: High daily volume: partitions enable parallel processing
cons: Seasonal capacity: partition sizing needs tuning

alternatives.label: Data pipeline per data set
pros: Seasonal capacity: scale pipelines by data set
cons: High daily volume: separate pipelines add overhead

alternatives.label: No parallel data processing
cons: High daily volume: processing remains serial

decisions.rationale: High daily volume decides in favor of partitioning to enable parallel processing. This costs tuning effort as volume changes seasonally.
consequences: The pipeline must partition and coordinate document work.
Partition sizing may need seasonal adjustment.

decisions.decision: How should model quality be monitored in production?
decisions.context: Operators need to see when classification quality drifts, so the system needs production monitoring that surfaces model performance changes.

alternatives.label: Model performance monitoring
pros: Detect quality drift: observe model performance

alternatives.label: Monitoring or logging data and predictions
pros: Operational visibility: logs inputs and predictions
cons: Detect quality drift: logs alone may not measure quality

alternatives.label: No in-production monitoring
cons: Detect quality drift: no production signal

decisions.rationale: Detect quality drift decides in favor of monitoring model performance. It requires defining performance measures and may require labeled outcomes to assess quality.
consequences: Operators need performance measures and drift thresholds.
Quality signals must be made available to operators.

decisions.decision: How should predictions be served to consuming teams?
decisions.context: Several teams consume classification results, while the brief does not specify synchronous access or a latency requirement. Batch results in shared storage provide a simple fit for scheduled processing and multiple consumers.

alternatives.label: Data batch based model serving
pros: High daily volume: process and publish batches
cons: Multiple consuming teams: consumers wait for batch output

alternatives.label: Microservice based model serving
pros: Multiple consuming teams: distributed real-time access
cons: High daily volume: online serving capacity required

alternatives.label: Hybrid online/offline model serving
pros: Multiple consuming teams: supports online and batch consumers
cons: High daily volume: operates two serving paths

decisions.rationale: High daily volume and the absence of a stated real-time requirement decide in favor of batch serving. This gives up immediate results and assumes teams can consume published batches.
consequences: Results are written to storage for team consumption.
Consumers must handle batch availability and timing.

Quality metric, source of ground truth, and drift thresholds
Whether monitoring should trigger human review, retraining, or model replacement
